major_event: Goldfinch Prime wind-down, full Prime investor redemption, contract pause, and transition of the legacy protocol to maintenance mode for borrower recoveries

duplicate_check.notes: No Goldfinch or Goldfinch Prime canonical platform was found in the current repository review. A full candidate audit remains required before any promotion.

notes: The first-party governance proposal moves the legacy Goldfinch protocol into recovery-only maintenance mode and winds down Goldfinch Prime. A 7 July update states that Prime investors were fully redeemed, no new deposits are accepted, and the contract was paused, while legacy V1 borrower pools remain in payment or recovery. CYA focuses on CeFi and does not prioritize DeFi lending protocols in its initial scope, so this is staged for an explicit scope and entity-boundary decision rather than forced into canonical data. Review whether Goldfinch Prime should be modeled as a historically significant institutional-yield product/platform exception, whether legacy V1 and Prime remain one platform entity, and how customer outcomes should be scoped by product.

major_event: Platform-wide orderly wind-down with Earn, staking, lending, and other products scheduled for phased discontinuation and product-specific redemption or settlement arrangements still pending

duplicate_check.notes: No BitMart canonical CYA platform was found in the current repository review. A full candidate audit remains required before any promotion.

notes: BitMart announced an orderly wind-down on 26 July 2026. The notice schedules the end of spot, futures, and other trading on 26 August 2026 and formal trading-platform termination on 31 January 2027. It also states that BitMart Earn, Staking, Lending, Launchpad, and other products will be discontinued in phases, with dedicated redemption, settlement, and follow-up procedures to be communicated to affected users. Generic exchange Earn products are not prioritized in CYA, so BitMart is staged rather than promoted. Review whether the platform-wide shutdown and unresolved product-level customer outcomes justify a historically significant exchange-Earn exception, identify each affected yield or lending product, preserve product-specific custody and terms, and do not infer repayment completion before official settlement evidence is available.

major_event: Orderly shutdown announced on 23 June 2023, interest accrual stopped immediately, bank withdrawals remained available until 7 July, crypto withdrawals until 31 July, and all services were scheduled to terminate on 31 July 2023

duplicate_check.notes: No canonical Pillow, Pillow Fund or pillow.fund platform was found in the repository review. The automated candidate audit and direct canonical JSON inspection remain required before promotion.

notes: Contemporaneous reports reproduce Pillow's customer notice that the company would close on 31 July 2023 because of regulatory uncertainty, that deposits and accrued interest were safe and available for immediate withdrawal, and that users should redeem and withdraw. Bank withdrawals were scheduled to end on 7 July and crypto withdrawals on 31 July. This supports an orderly voluntary/regulatory shutdown record, but does not prove that every customer completed withdrawal. Before canonical promotion, preserve the exact product and custody model, original URL history, and a conservative customer outcome rather than assuming universal full repayment.

major_event: Celsius-provided Bitcoin Interest Account withdrawals and new investments paused in June 2022, Celsius entered bankruptcy in July 2022, Nuri entered insolvency and closed its business by 19 December 2022, while ordinary bank, wallet and vault assets followed separate treatment

duplicate_check.notes: No canonical Nuri, Bitwala or Nuri Bitcoin Interest Account record was found. The automated candidate audit must also compare the product with the existing Celsius platform record without collapsing the customer-facing intermediary product into Celsius itself.

notes: Nuri, formerly Bitwala, launched the Bitcoin Interest Account with Celsius in May 2021. Nuri's own customer response stated that Celsius exclusively offered the product and Nuri brokered it. Withdrawals and new investments were paused after the Celsius halt. Nuri later filed for insolvency and discontinued all services on 19 December 2022, but ordinary bank balances, custodial wallet assets and self-custodial vaults were explicitly treated separately from the Celsius-linked interest account. Model the interest account as a product-scoped customer-facing record, preserve Celsius as the underlying contractual counterparty, and do not apply the safety or recoverability of ordinary Nuri accounts to the frozen interest-account claims. Current Nuri and Bitwala services are successor/reused brands and are not evidence that the historical interest account resumed.
